title_jp: {映画館|えいがかん}が{閉館|へいかん}？
context: Monday 23 November, {勤労感謝の日|きんろうかんしゃのひ}, a public holiday. レン is at his favourite small cinema in {長野市|ながのし} and finds a notice that it will close in March; on LINE he and アルちゃん talk about shrinking towns in Japan and Spain, and what if.
scene: A holiday morning. レン sends you a photo from his favourite cinema in {長野市|ながのし}: a notice on the door.

phrases.jp: {大雪|おおゆき|heavy snow|3}のため、{電車|でんしゃ}が{止まって|とまって}います。
phrases.en: Because of heavy snow, the trains are stopped.
phrases.note: Station and news style. A friend would say {雪|ゆき}がすごくて{電車|でんしゃ}{止|と}まってる.

phrases.jp: もし{僕|ぼく}がお{金持ち|かねもち|rich person|4}だったら、その{映画館|えいがかん}を{買う|かう}のに。
phrases.en: If I were rich, I'd buy that cinema.
phrases.note: もし〜たら、〜のに: a wish about something that isn't true. The のに adds 'if only'.

phrases.jp: {小さい|ちいさい}{町|まち}だと、すぐ{噂|うわさ|rumour, gossip|3}になるよね。
phrases.en: In a small town, things get around fast, right?
phrases.note: {噂|うわさ}になる = become gossip. {噂|うわさ}によると = rumour has it.

phrases.jp: もし{日本|にほん}に{住む|すむ}なら、{田舎|いなか|the countryside|4}と{都会|とかい|big city|3}、どっちがいい？
phrases.en: If you lived in Japan, which would you pick: the countryside or the city?
phrases.note: 〜なら: 'if (that's your plan)'. A classic small-talk question for foreigners.

phrases.jp: {人口|じんこう|population|3}が{減って|へって|to decrease|4}、お{店|みせ}がどんどん{閉まって|しまって|to close (shop, door)|4}います。
phrases.en: The population is falling, and shops keep closing one after another.
phrases.note: どんどん = steadily, more and more. You'll hear this about rural towns everywhere.

dialogue_setting: LINE, Monday 23 November, late morning. レン is in front of a small cinema in {長野市|ながのし}; you're on the {縁側|えんがわ} at the {田中|たなか} house.

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: おはよう。{今日|きょう}は{祝日|しゅくじつ|public holiday|3}だから、いつもの{映画館|えいがかん}に{来た|きた}んだけど…
dialogue.en: Morning. It's a holiday today, so I came to my usual cinema, but…

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: {入口|いりぐち}にこんな{紙|かみ}が。「{利用者|りようしゃ|users, customers|3}が{減少した|げんしょうした|decrease|2}ため、3{月末|がつまつ}で{閉館|へいかん|closing (a hall, for good)|2}いたします」
dialogue.en: There's a paper like this at the entrance: 'Due to a decrease in customers, we will close at the end of March.'
dialogue.note: Formal notice language: {減少|げんしょう}した = {減|へ}った, いたします = humble します.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: え、{本当|ほんとう}？レンさんがよく{行く|いく}{映画館|えいがかん}ですよね？
dialogue.en: What, really? That's the cinema you go to all the time, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: うん。もしここがなくなったら、どこで{古い|ふるい}{映画|えいが}{見れば|みれば}いいんだろう
dialogue.en: Yeah. If this place disappears, where am I supposed to watch old films?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: スペインの{村|むら|village|3}も、{人口|じんこう|population|3}が{減って|へって|to decrease|4}お{店|みせ}がどんどん{閉まって|しまって|to close (shop, door)|4}ます
dialogue.en: Spanish villages too: the population is falling and shops keep closing.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: もし{僕|ぼく}がお{金持ち|かねもち|rich person|4}だったら、その{映画館|えいがかん}{買う|かう}のにｗ
dialogue.en: If I were rich, I'd buy that cinema lol

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: ｗ ありがとう。でも{正直|しょうじき}、{田舎|いなか|the countryside|4}の{町|まち}はちょっと{苦手|にがて}なんだ
dialogue.en: lol thanks. But to be honest, I'm not great with small country towns.

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: もし{小さい|ちいさい}{町|まち}に{住んでたら|すんでたら}、アプリも{使えなかった|つかえなかった}と{思う|おもう}。すぐ{噂|うわさ|rumour, gossip|3}になるから
dialogue.en: If I lived in a small town, I don't think I could have used the app. Word gets around fast.

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: だから…もし{長野市|ながのし}に{来る|くる}ことがあったら、{閉館|へいかん|closing (a hall, for good)|2}の{前|まえ}に{一緒|いっしょ}に{行かない|いかない}？
dialogue.en: So… if you ever come to {長野市|ながのし}, shall we go together before it closes?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: ぜひ！{雪|ゆき}で{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗れなかったら|のれなかったら}、ごめんなさいｗ
dialogue.en: I'd love to! Sorry in advance if the snow stops me getting on a train lol

listening.intro: That afternoon at {鷹ノ原|たかのはら} station you hear the announcement you'll hear all winter.

lines.jp: {大雪|おおゆき|heavy snow|3}のため、{長野|ながの}{行き|ゆき}の{電車|でんしゃ}は{30分|さんじゅっぷん}ほど{遅れて|おくれて}います。
lines.en: Because of heavy snow, the train for {長野|ながの} is running about 30 minutes late.

grammar.form: noun: + のため ({大雪|おおゆき}のため, {工事|こうじ}のため) · verb (plain): + ため ({減少|げんしょう}したため, {遅|おく}れたため) · い-adj: + ため ({寒|さむ}いため) · な-adj: + なため ({危険|きけん}なため)
grammar.explanation: A formal 'because', used in notices, announcements, news and work emails. Between friends it sounds stiff: say から or ので. Don't confuse it with ため meaning 'in order to' (〜するために): here it gives the cause.

examples.jp: {工事|こうじ|construction work|3}のため、この{道|みち}は{通れません|とおれません}。
examples.en: Due to construction work, this road is closed.

examples.jp: {道|みち}が{凍って|こおって|to freeze|3}いて{危険|きけん}なため、{今日|きょう}は{休校|きゅうこう|school closed|2}です。
examples.en: The roads are frozen and dangerous, so school is closed today.

quiz.question: {台風|たいふう|typhoon|3}の＿＿、{試合|しあい|match, game|3}は{中止|ちゅうし|cancellation|3}になりました。
quiz.en: Because of the typhoon, the match was cancelled.
quiz.explain: Noun + のため = because of. ので and から can't come straight after の like this.

quiz_more.question: {雪|ゆき}が{多い|おおい}＿＿、バスが{遅れて|おくれて}います。
quiz_more.en: Because there's a lot of snow, the buses are late.
quiz_more.explain: An い-adjective takes ため directly; の only comes after a noun.

quiz_more.question: この{道|みち}は{危険|きけん}＿＿ため、{通れません|とおれません}。
quiz_more.en: This road is dangerous, so you can't go through.
quiz_more.explain: A な-adjective keeps な before ため: {危険|きけん}なため.

kanji.where: On the paper taped to the cinema door in レン's photo, in big black letters.
kanji.breakdown: {閉館|へいかん}: 閉 close (a door inside the 門 gate) + 館 hall, building → 'the building closes'.
kanji.related: {開館|かいかん} = opening; {閉館時間|へいかんじかん} = closing time.

tip.title: Everyone knows your car
tip.body: In a small Japanese town people notice whose car is parked where and who came to visit. Worry about {人|ひと}の{目|め} (other people's eyes) is real, so many people keep dating private ({内緒|ないしょ}) until it's serious.

challenge.hint: He's being kind and patient. How do you thank him?
challenge.prompt: レン replies: 「{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}。もし{雪|ゆき}だったら、また{別|べつ}の{日|ひ}にしよう。{急がなくて|いそがなくて}いいよ」 You're touched that he's so patient. Which sticker?
challenge.explanation: ありがとう〜 is a warm, casual thanks for his kindness. {草|くさ} means 'lol' and would laugh off what he said, ガーン is shock, and {眠|ねむ}い… would sound like you want to end the chat.

vocab.note: {祝|しゅく} celebrate + {日|じつ} day. On calendars, often red.
{利用|りよう} use + {者|しゃ} person. Signs and notices; in speech: お{客|きゃく}さん.
Formal word for {減|へ}ること. News: {人口減少|じんこうげんしょう}. Opposite: {増加|ぞうか}.
Smaller than {町|まち}. Officially, Japan has {市|し}, {町|まち} and {村|むら}.
{人|じん} person + {口|こう} mouth: mouths to feed.
Opposite: {増|ふ}える. お{腹|なか}が{減|へ}った = I'm hungry (casual).
The shop closes by itself: {閉|し}まる. You close it: {閉|し}める.
Literally 'money holder'. もしお{金持|かねも}ちだったら = if I were rich.
Also one's rural hometown: {田舎|いなか}に{帰|かえ}る. Opposite: {都会|とかい}.
{噂|うわさ}になる = become gossip. {噂|うわさ}をすれば = speak of the devil.

kanji_study.parts: 氵 water radical + 咸 (all, every) → water draining away until all of it is gone: decrease.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 滅 (destroy): 減 has 口 inside, 滅 has 火 fire.

kanji_study.parts: Originally a person standing on top of a tree (木 at the bottom) → climbing up onto something: ride, get on.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 垂 (hang down): 乗 has the 木 tree shape at the bottom, 垂 ends in flat lines.

words.en: to give a ride; to put on

extras.title: Notice Japanese
extras.intro: Words you'll see taped to doors when something closes or changes.

items.jp: {本日|ほんじつ|today (formal)|3}{休業|きゅうぎょう|closed for business|2}
items.note: {本日|ほんじつ} is the formal {今日|きょう}.

items.jp: {臨時休業|りんじきゅうぎょう|unscheduled closure|2}
items.note: Closed for an unusual reason: illness, snow, repairs.

items.jp: {長い間|ながいあいだ}ありがとうございました
items.en: Thank you for all these years
items.note: The last line on a closing-down notice.

items.jp: ご{了承|りょうしょう|understanding, acceptance|2}ください
items.note: Polite way to say 'sorry, but that's how it is'.

items.jp: もし{雨|あめ}だったら、{家|いえ}にいる。
items.en: If it rains, I'll stay home.
items.note: 〜たら: the all-rounder, safe in most cases.

items.jp: {長野|ながの}に{行く|いく}なら、{善光寺|ぜんこうじ}がいいよ。
items.en: If you're going to {長野|ながの}, {善光寺|ぜんこうじ} is good.
items.note: 〜なら: reacting to someone's plan, giving advice.

items.jp: もっと{時間|じかん}があれば、{旅行|りょこう}できるのに。
items.en: If only I had more time, I could travel.
